text:
alex_support: Heads-up — Acme reported failures after creating an AWS Interface VPC Endpoint to our hosted/private API. App gets TLS handshake errors and 502s, started ~09:10 UTC. They attached curl output.
sara_networks: Can you paste the curl -v and a dig +short of the API hostname from inside their VPC? Also traceroute/tcptraceroute to the resolved IP.
alex_support: Pasting minimal repro from customer (SANITIZED):
```
$ dig +short api.acme-app.internal
10.0.12.45
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
*   Trying 10.0.12.45...
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (10.0.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* TLS error: SSL: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake failed
```

jordan_eng: Interesting — dig returns a private IP, so they have Private DNS resolving to endpoint ENI. That part seems ok. Two possibilities: (1) endpoint DNS is pointing at the right ENI but SG/NACL blocks TCP 443 or healthcheck response; (2) cert hostname mismatch if they hit a different service behind the endpoint.
sara_networks: Also check the VPC Endpoint state — if the service requires acceptance, the endpoint might be in `pendingAcceptance` on our side and not actually connected. alex, did you check `describe-vpc-endpoints` from their account?
alex_support: They ran: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-endpoint-id,Values=vpce-0abc1234` -> shows `State: available`. Not pending. ENIs present in 3 subnets.
sara_networks: OK. Next: Security group on the endpoint ENIs matters — interface ENIs use the endpoint's SG. Client traffic to 10.0.12.45 must be allowed by that SG inbound on 443. Many customers accidentally set SG to only allow SG from their own LB or limited CIDR. Can you get `describe-network-interfaces` or the endpoint SG id?
alex_support: SG is `sg-0a1b2c3d` — they say it's the default group (should allow all outbound). Customer ran `sudo iptables -L` no weird local blocks. NACLs are default (allow).
jordan_eng: Another common culprit: split-horizon DNS misconfiguration where Private DNS is enabled but resolves to the vpce IP in some AZs and to public IPs in others (cross-account or resolver rules). Ask them to run `dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @169.254.169.253` and also check from multiple AZ subnets. If any subnet gets public IP, traffic may egress and be blocked by egress allowlist.
alex_support: They ran dig from two subnets: us-east-1a -> 10.0.12.45, us-east-1c -> 34.200.11.22 (public). So yup, split answers.
sara_networks: That explains intermittent TLS errors and 502s — some AZs hit our private endpoint (works if SG/NACL ok), others go to public IP which may be blocked by their egress allowlist or transit GW/NAT. Action: ensure the VPC endpoint has Private DNS enabled and that there are no Route53 Resolver rules or Private Hosted Zones shadowing the name inconsistent across VPCs. Also confirm they don't have outbound proxy doing SNI rewrite.
jordan_eng: Quick repro tip for them: from a failing AZ, force the request to the vpce IP with SNI so they can validate cert chain:
```
curl --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:10.0.12.45 -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
```
If that works, then DNS mismatch/egress is the problem. If TLS still fails, capture `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.45:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -showcerts` and paste output.
alex_support: They tried the --resolve trick from the public-resolving AZ: it returned OK (200) when forced to the 10.0.12.45 IP. So DNS split-horizon confirmed.
sara_networks: Final checklist for customer: (1) Remove or update any Route53 private hosted zone or resolver rule that points the API name to public IPs in some AZs. (2) Ensure VPC Endpoint Private DNS setting is enabled for that endpoint. (3) If using Transit Gateway or shared resolver, ensure forward rules are consistent across attachs. (4) If service requires endpoint acceptance on our side, verify acceptance state (not the case here).
jordan_eng: Also noted: if they use custom certs or custom domain mapped at CloudFront, PrivateLink won't automatically map the custom domain — they'd need to ensure SNI and cert SANs align at the service side.

alex_support: Action items: ping customer with steps and ask for traceroutes from both AZs, and to check Route53 resolver rules. I'll mark as high priority and follow up. :thumbsup:
